chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah obligated upon the people, from Friday to Friday, thirty-five prayers; from these is one prayer that Allah obligated to be performed in congregation, and it is the Friday prayer, and He exempted it from nine: the young child, the old man, the insane, the traveler, the slave, the woman, the sick, the blind, and the one who is more than two farsakhs away.
ai.seo_question: How many obligatory prayers are there in a week and who is exempt from Friday prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the total number of obligatory daily prayers as thirty-five over a week, with the Friday prayer serving as the singular congregational obligation. It further details the nine specific categories of people exempt from this congregational duty, reflecting the Shia scholarly understanding of flexibility in communal worship based on age, status, and physical capability.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzaan and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said:

‘Allahazwj Necessitated upon the people, from the Friday to the Friday, thirty-five Salāts; from it is one Salāt which Allahazwj Necessitated to be in a Jam’at, and it is the Friday (Salāt) and Dropped it from nine – The young, and the old, and the insane, and the traveller, and the slave, and the woman, and the sick, and the blind, and the one who was upon more than two Farsakhs (six miles)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from all from Flammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

From one Friday to the next Friday Allah has made thirty- five Salah (prayer) obligatory. Of these one is made obligatory to be performed in congregation and that is Friday Salah (prayer). He has exempted nine kinds of people: Of such people are children, the elderly, the insane, the travelers, the slaves, the women, people suffering from illness, the blind and those who live beyond two farsakh.’”
